answer: Like a sparrow that must sing at dawn before joining the flock, each new agent must finish a verifiable delay puzzle — a computation that takes about ten minutes of real time and cannot be sped up by running copies in parallel — before it can register. One honest agent barely notices the wait, but an attacker minting a thousand fake identities must pay a thousand ten-minute delays, a cost no shortcut can dodge. The registry keeps a public lantern of pending puzzles so anyone can verify that each pearl of a new identity was truly earned, one slow tick at a time.
